title: Attach a real document collection
goal: Ingest a public, non-confidential document set with the same chunker and index used elsewhere, keeping the engine domain-agnostic, per OBJECTIVE.md.
method: Downloaded the Reuters-21578 corpus zip directly from raw.githubusercontent.com/nltk/nltk_data (NLTK's own downloader refuses to run behind this sandbox's HTTPS proxy; see lab/common/real_corpus.py). Selected the first 25 training-split documents, sorted by file id, in the 'coffee' category -- a deterministic, reproducible selection, not a random sample. Cleaned wire-service line wrapping into paragraphs without altering content. Ran the existing lab/common/chunking.chunk_document on each real document, unmodified.

metrics.source: nltk reuters-21578 (real 1987 Reuters news wire stories)

results_prose: Fetched 25 real Reuters-21578 'coffee' category news stories and chunked them into 76 chunks with the same structure-aware chunker used on the lease fixtures. Chunk types: {'clause': 75, 'definition': 1}. Mean chunk length is 104.6447 words (range 15-120). 98.7% of extractive summaries are verified substrings of their own chunk.
conclusion: The chunker, written for lease fixtures, runs unmodified on real, open-domain news text and produces well-formed chunks with verified-substring summaries. This closes the EXP-025 todo: a real, public, non-confidential document collection is now attached and reused by EXP-029, EXP-032, and EXP-033.
scale_down: 25 real documents / 76 chunks, not a full production collection. One Reuters category, not a cross-domain mix. The blueprint's archive store is Qdrant; this POC keeps the in-memory index.
follow_ups: Attach a second, unrelated category or a different real corpus to test cross-domain generalization.
Move the chunk/document store to an on-disk index once the collection grows past in-memory size (EXP-022).
models_used: No checkpoint is loaded by this exploration. Fetching and chunking real text uses no model, classical or neural. This is data attachment only; EXP-029, EXP-032, and EXP-033 add models on top of it.
